_doc: Prose descriptions of what each benchmark's invention DOES, for NotebookLM. Proven 2026-08-31: this form finds a champion the feature-checklist question rejects, at every roster size 10-30, and correctly answers NONE when no candidate qualifies. A checklist over feature NAMES does not work (core rescue, 25%); a description of the MECHANISM does. Each must end with the NONE escape or a chunk with no qualifying document forces a false pick.

10.label: two microwave power supplies feeding two tiers (NO frequency condition — T10-2)
10.question:
All the attached candidates concern wireless systems that send power and/or data without cables. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: it delivers power BY MICROWAVE OR RF, WIRELESSLY, to TWO different units of the same chain — one feed powering a sensor unit, a SECOND, SEPARATE feed powering the relay/repeater unit that the sensor communicates with. The point is that BOTH tiers are powered wirelessly by their own transmitter, not just one of them.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.

13.label: PURPOSE form: replace the tethered signal generator — wake a battery pack from a phone instead of a wired console
13.question:
All the attached candidates concern battery packs, battery management, or equipment that communicates with them. At most ONE of them solves THIS PROBLEM: normally, to wake up a battery pack and make it start delivering power — for testing, servicing or teaching — an operator must physically connect a bulky WIRED signal generator or programmer to the pack and press buttons on it. The invention gets rid of that tethered console: the operator instead sends the command from an ordinary phone, tablet or PC over a RADIO link to a small unit, and that unit turns the command into the battery's own wired bus language and delivers it to the pack's management electronics, so the battery starts up and outputs power. The POINT is replacing the physically-connected signal generator with a wireless command path, so no operator has to stand at the pack with a wired box.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>

14.label: charge-state curve across the CC/CV switch vs a beginning-of-life reference (NO inflection wording — T14-2/3)
14.question:
All the attached candidates concern charging batteries and judging their condition. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: while charging, it records how the battery's state or voltage develops ACROSS the point where the charger switches from constant-current to constant-voltage, COMPARES that against a stored reference recorded when the battery was NEW, turns the difference into a measure of how far the battery has degraded, and USES that measure to change how much the battery is charged. The point is the comparison against a beginning-of-life reference feeding back into the charging.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>

12.label: already-chilled air from inside the water-cooled power supply, redirected to the jig, to stop condensation
12.question:
All the attached candidates are battery charging/discharging equipment with cooling. At most ONE of them takes air that has ALREADY been chilled inside its water-cooled power-supply enclosure and redirects that air to the charging jig, so that the enclosure is kept free of CONDENSATION and the jig is cooled as a by-product. The others cool by some different means.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>

13_component_form_FAILED.label: wireless data in, wired CAN/LIN out to a BMS, in one unit (NO trigger clause — T13-2)
13_component_form_FAILED.question:
All the attached candidates concern battery systems, battery management, or wireless communication with equipment. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: a SINGLE unit contains BOTH a wireless radio module (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, 5G, LoRa or similar) that receives data from a user's terminal, AND a controller that sends that data onward over a WIRED vehicle-style bus — CAN or LIN — into a battery pack's own management electronics (BMS/BMU). The point is the bridge inside one box: radio in, wired bus out to the battery's own controller.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.

10_v2.label: the RELAYING node is itself fed by beamed power (no 'two separate supplies', no frequency condition)
10_v2.question:
All the attached candidates concern wireless systems that move power and/or data without cables. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: it sends power THROUGH THE AIR OVER A DISTANCE — as a beamed or radiated microwave/RF wave, not through a plug and not through a coil held against the device — to an INTERMEDIATE wireless node that RELAYS another device's measurements onward, so that the relaying node itself needs no wiring and no battery to replace. Feeding only the end sensor this way is NOT enough: the node that FORWARDS the data must itself be powered by the beamed wave.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>
10_v2.why: v1 required TWO separate power-supply devices, one per tier, and recovered 2 of t10's 5 rejected champions. v2 states the mechanism — the relay is itself beam-powered — without prescribing how many transmitters do it, and widens the power vocabulary per F3f.

13_v2.label: conversion of a radio-borne command into the battery's own wired bus signalling (no 'one box', no operator narrative)
13_v2.question:
All the attached candidates concern battery packs, battery management electronics, or equipment that communicates with them. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: a command that ARRIVES OVER A RADIO LINK is CONVERTED into the wired signalling that a battery's own management electronics speak — a vehicle-style differential two-wire bus such as CAN or LIN — and is then driven onto that wired bus into the battery's management unit. The point is the CONVERSION between a wireless command and the battery's own wired bus signal. A system that merely reports battery data outward over radio, or that is wired end to end, does NOT qualify.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>
13_v2.why: v1-component required the radio and the bus driver inside ONE unit (5 picks, 1 champion, two unread candidates at opus 2.0/3.0); v1-purpose wrapped it in an operator/workflow story and returned 0 picks in 780 while REJECTING the known champion CN117692268. v2 keeps only the protocol conversion.

14_v2.label: during-charge curve vs the battery's own as-new stored curve, fed back into charging (no CC/CV switch, no inflection)
14_v2.question:
All the attached candidates concern charging batteries and judging their condition. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: while the battery is being charged, it COMPARES the curve the battery traces during that charge against a STORED curve recorded from the SAME battery when it was NEW, turns the difference between the two into a number expressing how far the battery has aged, and then USES that number to change how the battery is charged. The point is the comparison against the battery's own as-new reference, feeding back into the charging itself. Measuring degradation without changing the charging, or changing the charging without an as-new reference, does NOT qualify.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>
14_v2.why: v1 tied the comparison to the CC-to-CV switchover point; the inflection wording had already been measured at 2/7 on the core rescue. v2 drops the switchover and the inflection entirely and keeps the as-new reference comparison plus the feedback into charging.

_lesson_v2: 2026-09-03: v2 questions for t10/t13/t14 are re-pitched per the 09-02 finding that the variable is OVER-SPECIFICATION, not framing. Each drops one over-tight element (t10 two separate supplies · t13 one-box packaging and the operator story · t14 the CC/CV switchover and inflection) and keeps the mechanism at the abstraction the corpus can satisfy. Validation is free: the rejected piles already hold opus-scored champions — t10 5, t13 4, t14 8 — so recall is measured against verdicts already paid for. Questions were written from the BENCHMARK's own feature list, never from the champions' texts, so the controls stay honest.

10_v3.label: BOTH tiers fed by beamed power, any grade, any number of transmitters (v1 core relation, incidentals relaxed)
10_v3.question:
All the attached candidates concern wireless systems that move power and/or data without cables. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: in the SAME installation, BOTH the sensing unit AND the intermediate unit that relays the sensor's readings onward receive their operating power as a wave sent THROUGH THE AIR OVER A DISTANCE — beamed or radiated microwave/RF, not a plug and not a coil held against the device. It does not matter whether ONE transmitter or two supply that power, nor which words the document uses (microwave, RF, radiated, beamed, far-field). What matters is that BOTH tiers are fed this way, and a document counts even if it describes this only partially.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>
10_v3.why: v2 changed the CORE RELATION and narrowed it (relay only, sensor insufficient) and lost CN103683526. v3 restores v1's relation — BOTH tiers fed — and relaxes only the INCIDENTALS: the number of supply devices, the vocabulary, and the grade. The core rescue measured t10's satisfiable core as 'both supplies, ANY grade', and CN103683526 owns both only at PARTIAL.

13_v3.label: component form with the one-box packaging relaxed (v1-component core relation, incidental dropped)
13_v3.question:
All the attached candidates concern battery systems, battery management, or wireless communication with equipment. At most ONE of them does this specific thing: a wireless radio module (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, 5G, LoRa or similar) receives data sent from a user's terminal, AND a controller puts that data onto a WIRED vehicle-style bus — CAN or LIN — that runs into a battery pack's own management electronics (BMS/BMU), so the pack's own controller receives it. Whether these parts sit in one housing or in several separate boxes does NOT matter, and neither does what the pack does afterwards. What matters is the path: radio in from a terminal, wired CAN/LIN bus out into the battery's management electronics.
Identify it. If no attached document does this, answer exactly NONE.
Reply on one line: PICK: <publication number or NONE> — <one line why>
13_v3.why: Of three t13 wordings only the component form ever recovered a champion (CN117692268, 1/4); v2's conversion-only abstraction found 0 and its novel picks scored 1.0/1.0. v3 restores that relation verbatim and drops ONLY its incidental packaging constraint ('a SINGLE unit contains BOTH'), per the t14 lesson.

_lesson_v3: 2026-09-04 CORRECTED LESSON: t14's v2 worked because it relaxed an INCIDENTAL constraint (where on the charge curve the comparison is observed) while leaving the core relation fully specified. It did NOT delete the previously-measured inflection wording — v1 had already dropped that. t10 v2 and t13 v2 both failed because they CHANGED THE CORE RELATION (narrowing it and generalising it respectively). Rule: relax incidentals — measurement locus, packaging, actor, device count, vocabulary, grade — never the core relation. n=3, working rule not a law.
